# mockingbird

> Local emulators. Real API contracts. Mockingbird provides stateful emulators for third-party APIs and SQL databases. Use vendor-compatible request and response shapes, persistent in-memory state, and deterministic controls in Node, Bun, browsers, and Workers. Every HTTP emulator is a Fetch handler (`createRuntime().fetch(request) → Promise<Response>`) published to npm as `@crvouga/mockingbird-service-<name>`. Every emulator is isomorphic and runs in Node >= 22, Bun >= 1.2, browsers, and Workers.

Install emulators as devDependencies; each package is self-contained. Prefer injecting the emulator's `fetch` in-process; when a URL is required, run `npx mockingbird-<service> serve` (or `createServer` from `./server`); every HTTP service answers `GET /__admin/health`, `/__admin/*` (including `GET /__admin/state` and `GET /__admin/ui`) and `x-mockingbird-namespace`. All internal paths use the configurable `adminPrefix` (CLI `--admin-prefix`, env `MOCKINGBIRD_ADMIN_PREFIX`), including namespace URLs `/__admin/ns/<name>/…`; there are no unprefixed health or namespace aliases. Read the README of each package you use — it is the integration guide for coding agents (also shipped in `node_modules/<package>/README.md`).

The sentence above is the product's identity. The rules for the mark, the colors, and where that sentence has to appear: [Design](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/crvouga/mockingbird/main/docs/DESIGN.md).

Each service declares its own parity: a short statement of the vendor surface it keeps in step. Read that statement, and the package README, before you depend on an emulator.

## Admin controls

Every HTTP emulator takes the same controls, and each means the same thing at boot (`createRuntime({ adminControls })`, `serve --admin-controls`), over `/__admin`, and in a request header: isolate state by key (`x-mockingbird-namespace`), reset to boot (`POST /__admin/reset`), snapshot and restore (`POST /__admin/snapshots`), move the clock (`POST /__admin/clock`, `x-mockingbird-time`), inject faults (`POST /__admin/faults`, `x-mockingbird-fault`), and add latency or timeouts (`PUT /__admin/latency`, `x-mockingbird-delay`, `x-mockingbird-timeout`). The same seed and the same requests give the same bytes. `GET /__admin` on a running emulator lists every route and header.

- [Admin controls](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/crvouga/mockingbird/main/docs/ADMIN_CONTROLS.md): where each control is, the three ways to set one, and what holds for all of them.
- [Namespaces](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/crvouga/mockingbird/main/docs/admin-controls/NAMESPACES.md): A namespace is an isolation key. Each key has its own records, clock, random streams, faults, latency, journal, metrics and snapshots, so parallel test workers share one emulator without seeing each other.
- [Reset](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/crvouga/mockingbird/main/docs/admin-controls/RESET.md): Reset returns a namespace to exactly the state it booted in: records, ids, clock, seed, faults, latency, snapshots, journal and metrics. A reset namespace cannot be told apart from a new one, which is what makes a test independent of the tests before it.
- [Snapshot and restore](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/crvouga/mockingbird/main/docs/admin-controls/SNAPSHOT_AND_RESTORE.md): A snapshot is a saved copy of a whole namespace. Take one after setting up the state a test needs, and restore it before each test: the namespace goes back to exactly that state, so the requests that follow give the same responses every time.
- [Clock](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/crvouga/mockingbird/main/docs/admin-controls/CLOCK.md): Every timestamp an emulator writes reads from its clock. Set it, freeze it or move it, and expiries, retry windows and renewals arrive in milliseconds instead of being waited for.
- [Checkpoints and branches](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/crvouga/mockingbird/main/docs/admin-controls/CHECKPOINTS_AND_BRANCHES.md): Every successful write checkpoints the namespace. Read the namespace as it was at any checkpoint, or branch from one and take a different path, without touching the main line.
- [Faults](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/crvouga/mockingbird/main/docs/admin-controls/FAULTS.md): A fault makes the emulator fail on purpose: answer `503`, drop the connection, cut a response off mid-body, or hold it back. It is how a test reaches a vendor's failure modes without the vendor.
- [Latency and timeouts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/crvouga/mockingbird/main/docs/admin-controls/LATENCY_AND_TIMEOUTS.md): Make responses slow, or make them never arrive. Latency is how long every request takes; a timeout holds a request and then drops it. With virtual time, the waits are spent on the mock clock and cost no test time.
- [Seed and determinism](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/crvouga/mockingbird/main/docs/admin-controls/SEED_AND_DETERMINISM.md): Given the same boot controls and the same requests in the same order, an emulator answers the same bytes: ids, timestamps, which requests a fault hits, jitter, and the journal. The seed is what fixes every random choice.
- [The control document](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/crvouga/mockingbird/main/docs/admin-controls/CONTROL_DOCUMENT.md): Every control is described once, as JSON. The same document boots an emulator, is read and written over the admin API, and is what the request headers stand for. This page is its schema.
- [Boot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/crvouga/mockingbird/main/docs/admin-controls/BOOT.md): An emulator starts with whatever controls you give it. That starting point is also what a reset returns to.
- [Request headers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/crvouga/mockingbird/main/docs/admin-controls/REQUEST_HEADERS.md): A request can carry its own controls. Nothing needs to be set up first, and a client that can only set default headers still reaches every control.
- [Journal, metrics and state](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/crvouga/mockingbird/main/docs/admin-controls/JOURNAL_AND_STATE.md): Three ways to see what an emulator did and what it holds: the journal lists every request it received, metrics count them, and state reads and edits the stored rows directly.
- [Reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/crvouga/mockingbird/main/docs/admin-controls/REFERENCE.md): Every admin route, every control header, the error shape and how access is guarded, on one page. Each row links to the page that defines it.

## Reporting issues and requesting services

Do not work around an emulator in your own project: file a GitHub issue on crvouga/mockingbird and your fix lands in the next release. Search first (`gh issue list --repo crvouga/mockingbird --state all --search "<service> <operation>"`), redact every key and all personal data, fill in the kind's template, and run `gh issue create --repo crvouga/mockingbird --title "<title>" --label agent-reported,<kind> --body-file issue.md`. Feature and service requests are specifications: list the operations you call and number the behaviors you need as Given / When / Then; each becomes an acceptance test.

- [Filing guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/crvouga/mockingbird/main/docs/REPORTING_ISSUES.md): when to file, redaction rules, reproduction and behavior formats, and what happens after.
- [Parity mismatch](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/crvouga/mockingbird/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/parity.md): title `[<service>] parity: <what diverges>`. The emulator and its oracle (vendor sandbox or real engine) answer the same requests differently.
- [Missing feature](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/crvouga/mockingbird/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature.md): title `[<service>] feature: <what is missing>`. An emulator lacks an operation, parameter, event, behavior or test control you use.
- [Bug](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/crvouga/mockingbird/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug.md): title `[<service>] bug: <what breaks>`. An emulator crashes, leaks state, contradicts its README, or does not build.
- [New service](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/crvouga/mockingbird/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/new-service.md): title `[new-service] <Vendor>: <API surface>`. No package emulates a vendor you depend on; describe the surface, auth, state, behaviors, webhooks and test controls you need.

## Fleet management

- [@crvouga/mockingbird-fleet](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/crvouga/mockingbird/main/packages/adapters/fleet/README.md): Vendor-neutral Node.js fleet lifecycle, installed-service loading, control client, discovery and archives. This is tooling, not a vendor emulator.
